info.name: TCOS Finance Tracking — Project & Source (chompoo)
info.description:
The 10 Project/Source endpoints from this split — POST /projects, PATCH/DELETE /projects/:id, PATCH/DELETE /tags/:id, PATCH/DELETE /departments/:id, POST /projects/:id/sources, PATCH/DELETE /sources/:id. See docs/backend/03-api-spec.md §6.

Self-contained: includes its own Login request. Run order 1→6 for a full create→update→delete cycle against a fresh project+source you create yourself. Requests 7-10 (tag/department update/delete) use the project's *already-seeded* tag/department (from supabase/seed.sql) since bulk-creating tags/departments (#23/#27) isn't part of this PR and is still mocked — see each request's own description for what that means for the delete ones.

**Access control note**: these routes still go through requireScope(...), which stays mock-permissive (any authenticated user passes) pending the StaffDept-backed real scope system — same known gap as GET /auth/me's `scope`. Not specific to this collection.

request.description:
Not one of the 10 endpoints — a harmless request to hang these notes on.

1. Run "1. Login" first — sets `access_token`.
2. Run 2→6 in order for a clean create→update→(create source)→update→delete→delete cycle on a project you create yourself — nothing pre-existing gets touched.
3. `tag_id`/`department_id` default to real seeded rows (Sponsorship Booth tag, IT department) so 7-10 work immediately without any manual DB setup. Update (7, 9) is fully safe to run — it's a rename, reversible. Delete (8, 10) will correctly 409 against these specific seeded rows (the IT department has live members, the tag/department's project has other stuff attached) — that's real, expected behavior demonstrating the dependency check, not a bug. To see the delete *success* path, insert a throwaway tag/department directly via SQL first and point these variables at it.

exec: pm.test('login failed — see response body', () => pm.expect.fail(pm.response.text()));

request.description: #18 — sets `created_project_id` for the rest of this collection.
#20 — total_income/total_expense are rejected here even if you add them to the body, that's real and intentional, not a bug to work around.

#34 — `type: spon` needs no `reference_id` (only `enroll`/`merch` do) and `actual_amount` mirrors `expect_amount` immediately since there's no approval step for sponsor money. Sets `created_source_id`.
#35 — actual_amount/type/reference_id/project_id are rejected here even if added to the body, that's real, not a bug.
#36 — 204. Run this before "11. Delete Project" — a project with a live source attached 409s.
#24 — `tag_id` defaults to the real seeded "Sponsorship Booth" tag. Safe, reversible rename.

#25 — the seeded tag is referenced by the seeded "Booth Sponsor A" source (and possibly a reimbursement), so this genuinely 409s TAG_HAS_DEPENDENTS against it. That's the real dependency check working, not broken — see "6. Delete Source" above for what a successful 204 looks like on a tag/source you actually control.
#28 — `department_id` defaults to the real seeded IT department. Safe, reversible rename.

#29 — the seeded IT department has live members (mark, fah), so this genuinely 409s DEPARTMENT_HAS_DEPENDENTS. Real dependency check, not a bug — to see a 204, insert a throwaway department with no members via SQL and point `department_id` at it.

#21 — 204, assuming "6. Delete Source" already ran (this project never had any tags/departments attached, only the source). Try it against a project that still has something attached to see PROJECT_HAS_DEPENDENTS for real.
